analysis:
This batch is documentation only: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/autopilot-placements-and-busy-reasons.md, head lines 1-9) and a paragraph added to docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 351-356). No executable code is in the supplied units, so I found no concrete security regression in these changes.

The changelog describes behavior the threat model should track, but the implementing source is not supplied:
- Autopilot now serves every verified downloaded catalog model, not only the saved selection (line 3).
- Autopilot downloads catalog models on the operator's behalf, on by default, persisting state in autopilot-downloads.json (line 4). This adds a network and disk surface with a 50 GiB free-disk floor. It is gated by saved Autopilot consent and a verified catalog build, and it never loads a model or deletes files.
- An adopted model keeps serving after its operation's control lease ends (line 5), and a hold can last up to 24 hours (line 6). These relate to A-016 and T-053, because serving continues without a live lease. The text says adoption ends on consent revocation, a failed weight-hash check, unload and restart, but I cannot verify that.
- A watchdog cancels stalled operations and preloads (line 8).
- Heartbeats gain optional fields reporting busy reasons and adopted and held models (line 7). This relates to T-058, because it adds disclosure to the coordinator, which is trusted.

The hardware-support.md addition says held slots are excluded from eviction snapshots and receive no reclaim credit in free_for_load_gb. The effect is that a held model can make other loads fail with capacity refusal, so there is a bounded availability trade-off. Another operation can still unload a held model.

Open questions for the next review pass, if code is supplied, mainly ProviderLoop adoption and hold code, the autopilot downloader and the heartbeat encoding:
1. Whether adoption is revoked on revocation, expiry and epoch changes (T-053, A-016).
2. Whether downloads verify catalog hashes, size and signature before joining the serving set (T-012, T-027, A-004).
3. Whether the downloads default-on setting is bounded without limits, which is disk-fill DoS (T-016).
4. Whether the new heartbeat fields stay within the existing privacy posture.
